description: A task's body may be a whole Snowflake Scripting block, not only a single statement - live-verified for a plain BEGIN...END, one with its own DECLARE section, and one nesting another block; the stored body reads back through the SHOW TASKS definition cell. The block is written UNQUOTED, exactly like the unquoted procedure body: a $$-quoted body is a syntax error at the dollar-quoted token. Once it is a body the block obeys the ordinary scripting rules, so a statement inside it that lacks its terminating semicolon is refused. Converted 1:1 from features/TaskBlockBodyTest (now retired).

steps.sql:
CREATE TASK block_task
WAREHOUSE = 'COMPUTE_WH'
SCHEDULE = '60 MINUTES'
AS
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO task_target VALUES (1);
END;

CREATE TASK quoted_task
WAREHOUSE = 'COMPUTE_WH'
SCHEDULE = '60 MINUTES'
AS $$
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO task_target VALUES (3);
END;
$$

CREATE TASK unterminated_task
WAREHOUSE = 'COMPUTE_WH'
SCHEDULE = '60 MINUTES'
AS
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO task_target VALUES (4)
END;
